items.gist: Puja is the gathering of differentiated states into the free, pure, infinite Bhairava-consciousness; consciousness itself is twelvefold and all-inclusive.
Consciousness appears in four forms (knower, knowing, instrument, known) and is mapped onto cakras in the white and red regions of the eye.
Paired cakras interact like yoni and linga, releasing amrita; above them stands the sahasrara, from which the brahmanda arises.
Soma flows through the cakras and is reabsorbed by Hamsa; the practitioner ascends toward the Brahma-state where fire and moon are equal.
Soma is heated and split, flowing downward through ankle, knee, and other centers, generating the cakra sequence up to brahmanda-vision.
The fourfold sequence in the aksha is summarized; Devi stands as consciousness, both inner and outer, and initiates creation.
Devi turns outward for creation, inward for stasis, and produces obstruction-like doubt for dissolution, then dissolves states into her own fire.
Dissolved states are recognized as grasped by her; residual doubt recondenses into new states, which consciousness again dissolves or condenses.
After enjoyment, the twelvefold group of karma, buddhi, and senses is withdrawn; ahamkara as instrument of identification is dissolved into the sun-like sense-field.
The agent is twofold, imagined and unimagined; both are dissolved through time-fire and great time into the all-pervasive consciousness.
All knowers, means, and objects are pure consciousness; the five kalanas—projection, knowledge, enumeration, movement, and sound—are described.
Pramatr-hood becomes manifest in the limit of consciousness; the principle of consciousness transcends both sequence and non-sequence.
